hints: Notice this question asks two separate things at once, how fast the reaction goes and how much product you get in the end.
Compare the acid concentrations first, 1.0 mol dm-3 versus 0.5 mol dm-3 at the same temperature, to decide which collision frequency is higher.
Now work out moles of HCl in each case with moles = concentration x volume, remembering marble is in excess so the acid limits the total product.
walkthrough:
**Separate rate from amount**

Think like a teacher with two questions in your head. Rate is about how often particles collide per second. Total product is about how many reacting particles you start with.

Reaction:
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{CaCl}_2 + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Decide the rate from concentration**

Temperature is the same at $40^{\circ}\text{C}$ and marble chips are in large excess both times. The only rate change is acid concentration falling from $1.0$ to $0.5$ mol dm$^{-3}$.

Lower concentration means fewer $\text{H}^+$ ions per cm$^3$, fewer successful collisions per second, so the second reaction is slower.

**Decide the total product from moles**

Because marble ($\text{CaCO}_3$) is in excess, hydrochloric acid is the limiting reagent. Use $n = c \times V$ with volume in dm$^3$.

First: $$n = 1.0 \times \frac{25}{1000} = 0.025 \text{ mol}$$
Second: $$n = 0.5 \times \frac{60}{1000} = 0.030 \text{ mol}$$

**Put it together**

More moles of limiting acid in the second experiment means more $\text{CO}_2$ and other products can form, even though it forms more slowly. That is slower rate plus greater final amount.

options.A: Incorrect. Faster is wrong because concentration is halved, so collision frequency falls. Less products is also wrong because moles of acid actually increase from 0.025 to 0.030 mol.
options.B: Incorrect. More products is right, but faster is wrong. Students who pick this focus only on the larger volume (60 cm3) and forget that rate depends on concentration, not total volume.
options.C: Incorrect. Slower is right, but less products is wrong. Students who pick this focus only on the lower concentration (0.5 mol dm-3) and forget to calculate total moles using volume as well.
options.D: Correct. Lower concentration gives a slower initial rate, but greater moles of HCl (0.030 mol vs 0.025 mol) with excess marble gives more total CO2 and other products.
